source_images_viewed.observation: Title, Siddhant Agrawal and Andrea R. Nahmod authors, and arXiv:2308.12926v1 24 Aug 2023 stamp agree with bound source.
Assumption 1.1 explicitly restricts to a bounded simply connected Jordan domain and gives positive constants c0,c1 bounding |Psi_z| for all z in the disc. This matches the report's hypotheses.

Assumption 1.1(2),(3) display the uniform homogeneous H^(1/2) trace and Hilbert-transform L-infinity bounds. Theorem 1.2 and Proposition 1.3 retain those hypotheses, with alpha>1/2 and the separate convex-domain alternative as reported.
Lemmas 4.2 and 4.3 display derivative bounds and det J_F=L_theta=G/c>0, matching the report's change-of-variable coverage.
Lemma 4.5 visibly has coefficient (4 g'(r)/r - 2 g(r)/r^2); the previous extraction candidate is excluded by the actual bound PDF, consistent with the prior HTML check.
The near-boundary proof splits separation relative to 1-|Y1|; Case 1 and the Case 2 threshold are visible. The reported distance-sensitive estimate corresponds to this page.
The probability normalization c-tilde |Psi_z|^2 dy, concavity/Jensen step E' <= C phi(E), and iteration to global uniqueness are visible, matching the report's bounded coverage.
Lemma 6.1 visibly assumes |dy/dt| <= c phi(y), and the preceding convex trace bound is present. No one-sided-derivative issue arises in this bound source.
